senses.gloss:
Jaivantāyana, ‘descendant of Jīvanta,’ is mentioned in the
Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad^1 as a teacher, with Śaunaka and
Raibhya, of Rauhiṇāyana.
1) iv. 5, 26 (Mādhyaṃdina). The name is recognised by Pāṇini, iv. 1, 103.

Jaivala or Jaivali, ‘descendant of Jīvala,’ is the patronymic
of Pravāhaṇa in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka^1 and Chāndogya Upani-
ṣads.^2 Jaivali, the king, in the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa^3
is the same person.
1) vi. 2, 1 (Kāṇva = vi. 1, 1 Mādhyaṃ-
dina), where the form is Jaivala.
2) i. 8, 1. 2. 8; v. 3, 1.
3) i. 38, 4.
